Bayern Munich's talisman delivered another fantastic showing against Arsenal, scoring a penalty and carrying the attack to show the Gunners exactly what they are missing at center forward

        Arsenal have long since moved past the stage where they want any more lessons from Harry Kane, and yet he insists on delivering them anyway. Though one of his counterparts in Arsenal blue might have played a critical role in the equalizer, this 2-2 draw came with indications aplenty of the value of a striker who can do it all.Like the North London derbies of old, Kane played the role of spoiler supreme for the Gunners, his 16th goal in 21 meetings an expertly struck penalty that capped an outstanding display from Bayern Munich's No. 9. The penalty he scored was the relatively easy part. Kane did plenty else. He had won that spot kick by finding space to meet Konrad Laimer's deflected drag back, Jurrien Timber making the fatal error of having arms while defending his penalty area in a UEFA-organized match.Scoring was not the half of what Kane brought tonight. Shorn of his primary running mates -- Luis Diaz fit enough only for the bench, Michael Olise suspended and Jamal Musiala still unavailable -- Kane took on even more of the creative burden. It is sometimes easy to think that any false nine can put up a dozen-plus assists to go alongside his goal a game when he is aiming for the best wide forwards. Today he was putting it on a plate for repurposed left back Alphonso Davies, his through ball delivering the sort of opening you'd back even the most agricultural defender (which Davies is not) to roll it in.With no Joshua Kimmich either, it fell on Kane to help out a youthful midfield with the ball progression too. Kimmich, Toni Kroos, Luka Modric: even the best ball-playing midfielders of their generation would have done well to ping what was effectively a goal kick following an Arsenal corner, a 70-yard pearler that pierced the best defense in the world in a flash.
This truly was a striker who could do it all, a worthy Ballon d'Or winner. As for his counterparts at Arsenal, they did their part. It should be noted that the Gunners would likely have suffered their first defeat in the league phase of the Champions League had it not been for a magnificently measured touch by Viktor Gyokeres with his back to goal, easing the ball into the path of Declan Rice, who thundered in a merited equalizer for the Premier League champions.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Kai Havertz too offered value of a sort. Arsenal were insistent that they would not play through Bayern's man-to-man press and would instead go over it. Havertz proved to be a valuable outlet in that regard, ensuring that Arsenal had a bit more of the territory, possession, shots and non-penalty xG. Mikel Arteta's game plan was a well-executed one, the sort that if replicated in the away leg of a big knockout tie at this ground, would have Arsenal firmly in the contest.Arsenal have proven once more that they belong in the inner tier of Champions League contenders, that a knockout tie between them and any of Bayern, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain might well be decided by the sort of "magic moment" that Arteta spoke of when eliminated at the Allianz Arena in 2024. Eberechi Eze and Rice delivered those, drilled efforts from tight angles to beat an otherwise impressive Manuel Neuer. Martin Odegaard was on song too with a brilliant assist for the opener. Bukayo Saka started brightly before what appeared to be a thigh injury.
And maybe Gyokeres' assist had a little bit of the supernatural to it. Stil, it is not the sort of magic you expect from the striker of a Champions League contender. Arsenal's strikers need to be scoring. Scratch that, they need to be shooting. Across 16 games in all competitions this season, the starting center forwards for the English champions have delivered 17 shots, 15 in 677 minutes for Kai Havertz and two in 330 for Viktor Gyokeres. On a per 90 basis, Arteta is getting slightly less shot production from his senior strikers as Nottingham Forest get from center back Murillo. It took Kane four games to take his 17th shot. Against admittedly inferior Bundesliga opposition to the average Premier League backline, Kane has 50 shots in 802 minutes.Arteta has always viewed his team as one where the shooting and scoring burden is shared around. When he challenged a player to score two or three goals a game it was Saka, not his center forwards. Arsenal's idealized striker was probably the fully fit Gabriel Jesus they had in the second half of 2022, a player who can drift from one flank to another, offering no fixed reference point and bringing others into play. Still, at peak fitness, Jesus averaged over three and a half shots per 90. He's a center forward. That's what they're supposed to do.Partly this may be a question of service. Arsenal's moves to goal have slowed right down this season, an average of 7.3 passes per scoring sequence, the longest in Europe's top five leagues. That is great for a late arriving Rice or even Odegaard, less so for the reference-point center forward. 
Arsenal will never play in a way that best suits Gyokeres in particular. Their opponents are generally packed so deep that there is not the space in the channel he craves. When they don't it is usually because they are applying the sort of suffocating press that makes it impossible to accurately release a striker over the top. Gyokeres might have loved Bayern's worst moments in the first half, when Odegaard got space to look up and ping passes in behind.Then again, no opponent plays in a way that suits Kane too. Ousmane Dembele and Raphinha will have every tactical adjustment imaginable put in place to negate them. Does anyone feel compelled to do that for Arsenal's attackers?Tonight Bayern's No. 9 had Ezri Konsa or Bruno Guimaraes tracking him high and low, ready to apply the blitz on one heavy touch. It never came. That is the difference between the best and what Arsenal have leading their line. They make the game suit them.

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a plethora of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.           Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

        Sam LaPorta is taking a unique approach in terms of his contract situation. Instead of keeping things in-house, LaPorta has chosen to publicly voice his displeasure. A former Pro Bowler, LaPorta is in the final year of his four-year, $9.47 million rookie contract. He is slated to earn $5.78 million in cash earnings this season. LaPorta, based on his comments, is clearly not happy that he has yet to receive a contract extension from the Lions. "I think the combination of like getting your heartstrings twisted, as well as the violent sport that we play, you know, it sucks and it's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take. "You know, like last year, whatever it was week nine, week 10. I break my f-----g back for the team, and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're not showing the love. "Yeah, it sucks. I'm going to continue to be a pro, and you know, I just a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. ... So I'm going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's gonna be all good. Yeah, I'll get paid somewhere else. So whatever." 
As he alluded to, LaPorta will likely have a big payday this offseason, whether it's with the Lions or someone else. His current market value is a three-year, $45.1 million deal, according to Spotrac. A former second-round pick, LaPorta has been a valuable part of the Lions' offense since he was drafted back in 2023. He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie and has caught 213 passes and 23 touchdowns in 47 regular season games. During the Lions' 2023 playoff run, he caught 21 of 27 targets for 176 yards and a score. LaPorta has bounced back this season after a serious back injury sidelined him for the second half of the 2025 campaign. He's been especially good over the past two games; he caught eight passes for 84 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 5 and caught each of his five targets for 88 yards and a score during last week's win over the Cardinals. It's very possible that the Lions -- and other potential teams that might be interested in his services -- are turned off by his decision to be so vocal about his contract status, especially with the Lions getting ready for a big showdown against the rival Packers. 
Talent, however, usually tops anything else in the NFL. As long as LaPorta continues to produce, he will surely have a robust market if he becomes a free agent this offseason. He has certainly made it clear that he is comfortable with the prospect of becoming a free agent for the first time this offseason if he and the Lions do not come to terms on a long-term deal.

title: Giants name JJ McCarthy starting QB for Week 7 game against Texans - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy is set to make his first career start for Big Blue

McCarthy is set to make his first career start for Big Blue

        The New York Giants have apparently made a decision on who their starting quarterback will be for this weekend's game against the Houston Texans. The plan is for JJ McCarthy to get the start, with Jameis Winston backing him up. McCarthy, who was traded from Minnesota earlier this season, is in line to make his first career start for the Giants, who are currently sitting atop the NFC East division with a 3-2-1 record. 
The Giants initially turned to Winston after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2. As he is known to do, Winston had both good and bad moments over the past five games. He played well enough, though, to post a 2-1-1 record as the Giants' starting quarterback. Winston struggled on this past Sunday, and he was replaced in the second half by McCarthy, who engineered three fourth-quarter scoring drives. The comeback fell short, however, as the Saints left New Jersey with a 34-27 win. 
"I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well. As we go forward here, this is going to be our direction. We think it gives us some good options on offense,'' John Harbaugh told reporters.Harbaugh chose McCarthy, who has displayed flashes of the player that compelled Minnesota to take him with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft. Injuries and inconsistent play, however, prevented McCarthy from having more success with the Vikings, who are off to a 5-0 start this season with Kyler Murray at quarterback. "I think he's a strong, young quarterback, has some experience in the National Football League," Harbaugh said of McCarthy shortly after the Giants traded for him. "Obviously, was a very high draft pick, very talented player and is going to make us a stronger football team."    
In 12 career games, McCarthy has completed just 57.2% of his passes with more interceptions (13) than touchdown passes (12). He has five touchdowns on the ground and an impressive 5.1 yards-per-carry average. "I think the last couple weeks, they've (the players) had a chance to see him practice and they're pretty fired up about it,'' Harbaugh said on Wednesday.Sunday's game was a microcosm of McCarthy's career up to this point. Despite having an underwhelming stat sheet, he was nonetheless able to engineer several successful scoring drives that got the Giants back in the game. 
McCarthy will face a Texans team that is finding its rhythm after a slow start to the season. 
The Texans, after a 0-4 start, have won two straight games after they defeated the Jaguars on Sunday in London. While this season hasn't been their best, the Texans have talented players on defense, especially pass rusher Will Anderson, who leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. While McCarthy's mobility may be an asset, his lack of experience running the Giants' offense could also hold the Giants back. Quarterback isn't the only position the Giants need to solidify.  They also need to figure out who the starting running back is after Cam Skattebo — the Giants' starter on paper — inexplicably received zero carries during Sunday's loss to the Saints. Harbaugh said afterward that he is waiting for one of his running backs to earn the job. That player will not be Najee Harris, who was released on Tuesday.

        The family of Hall of Fame basketball coach Bob Huggins said in a statement on Wednesday that the former Cincinnati, Kansas State and West Virginia coach is living with a "progressive cognitive condition" that is affecting his memory and daily aspects of his life. Huggins, who is the all-time winningest head coach in Cincinnati basketball history, is set to be inducted into the school's Hall of Fame class this week."Bob is living with a progressive cognitive condition that has begun to affect his memory, and aspects of his daily life," Huggins' family said in a statement. "While the family has chosen to keep this matter private over the past several months, they believe this is an appropriate time to share the news with the many people who have supported Bob throughout his remarkable career, particularly as he prepares to be honored with induction into the University of Cincinnati's James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame."
Huggins, 73, coached at Cincinnati from 1989 to 2005 and won 399 games with the school before coaching at Kansas State in 2006. After one season at Kansas State, Huggins took the West Virginia job and spent 16 seasons with the school, which included a Final Four appearance in 2010.Huggins initially resigned from his post at West Virginia and subsequently retired in 2023 after being arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol. However, months later, Huggins doubled down and claimed he never technically resigned from the school.
During his four-decade-long coaching career, Huggins won 934 games, including 345 during his time at West Virginia.

        Kurt Suzuki will not return as manager of the Los Angeles Angels, the team announced Wednesday. Suzuki had a club option for 2027 in his contract. He has been offered a special assistant position to remain in the organization. The 2026 season was Suzuki's only season as manager. He guided the Halos to a franchise record 100 losses, not that they were expected to contend."Kurt has earned tremendous respect in our clubhouse, and I've seen firsthand how much he cares about our players," interim GM John Mozeliak said in a statement. "I do not believe our record this year was a true reflection of his abilities as a manager. I'm pleased we were able to offer Kurt a role to stay on as a special assistant, where his knowledge of our players and his perspective would continue to be valuable to the organization."Suzuki, 43, was a special assistant to former Angels GM Perry Minasian from 2023-25 before taking over the managerial role this season. He had no prior coaching or managerial experience and the Angels gave him just a one-year contract, which is very unusual for a manager. Minasian was fired in June and replaced on an interim basis by Mozeliak."We haven't really dove deep into it," Suzuki told The Athletic in September when asked about his future and his conversations with Mozeliak. "We've had really good conversations about philosophies and stuff like that. We haven't really talked about next steps ... Would I like to be here? Of course I would."  Longtime Angels owner Arte Moreno agreed to sell the franchise to Stan Kroenke for $4 billion in September. Mozeliak has expressed an interest in taking over the team's baseball operations on a permanent basis, though he remains the interim right now. It is likely that position will be filled before the Angels look for a new manager.
Whoever replaces Suzuki will be the team's fifth full-time manager in six years, joining Joe Maddon (2020-22), Phil Nevin (2022-23), Ron Washington (2024-25), and Suzuki (2026). title: College Football Playoff tiers: Miami, Georgia lead contenders at midseason - CBS Sports
description: Sorting the nation's playoff hopefuls into tiers based on résumés, ceilings and remaining paths as we enter the s
body:
Sorting the nation's playoff hopefuls into tiers based on résumés, ceilings and remaining paths as we enter the season's second half
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Validation.As the only CBS Sports voter to have Miami at No. 1 before the season, I'll admit, the Hurricanes climbed to the top spot in the AP poll a few weeks before I expected them to after midseason carnage across the top 25. Miami is one of only six unbeatens left on the board, and it doesn't appear that anyone's safe moving forward during a year of extreme parity in the sport.We're sifting through the AP Top 25 to separate elites from the teams still selling themselves on potential in Week 8. There's a handful of true contenders who have already shown a championship ceiling against quality competition, while others need a large sample size before belonging in that conversation.Reputation gets you attention, but play on the field and execution are what truly qualify in front of the CFP selection committee. Here's where the nation's playoff hopefuls fall in our contender tiers, with championship credentials driving the discussion.Tier A.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Georgia (6-1) The Bulldogs' stock price shouldn't change after their home loss to Auburn. Three turnovers from Gunner Stockton were to blame, and the likelihood that happens again this season is slim. Kirby Smart mentioned after the game that he felt Georgia beat itself, and it's hard to disagree with that. The Bulldogs remain our SEC favorite at midseason and should get to the CFP as a top-4 seed.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami (6-0) Survival. That's what it's about for the Hurricanes throughout the duration of the season. Getting past Notre Dame on Nov. 7 is not a necessity, but it would virtually secure a top-4 seed in the bracket and an opening-round bye if they do. We're sticking with the season-long projection that Miami will be the Power Four's lone unbeaten on Selection Sunday and enter the CFP as the No. 1 seed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Notre Dame (6-1)Winning on the road is never easy. Doing it against a top-10 opponent is even more difficult. Notre Dame showed considerable fight at BYU after trailing 21-10 at halftime before taking a three-point lead in the fourth quarter prior to the Cougars' game-winning drive. The Fighting Irish are a better-executed goal-line play away from being unbeaten and ranked No. 1 in the AP poll, so it would be unwise to dismiss the Irish after one hiccup. That said, a loss to Miami in a couple of weeks severely alters Notre Dame's CFP outlook.
        
            
                Is Notre Dame in danger of missing CFP? Familiar conversation around Irish emerges after first loss of season
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Tier B.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    BYU (6-0) The best of the three unbeatens left in the Big 12, the Cougars catapulted themselves into the spotlight with the win over Notre Dame. Controversial ending aside, BYU earned it against a top-10 opponent with a victory that almost looked personal for Bear Bachmeier and his teammates. Can the Cougars bring that same level of swagger to UCF this weekend as a 6.5-point favorite or during their trip to Utah on Nov. 7? Those are two potential trouble spots for Kalani Sitake's squad.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indiana (6-1)I wonder how often Curt Cignetti smirks when he reads that this Indiana team isn't as good as his last one. Well, duh. It's hard to replicate a 16-0, record-setting season when you replace a Heisman-winning quarterback and several other top-end playmakers. However, through seven games, the Hoosiers are literally a foot from being unbeaten on a 23-game winning streak entering Saturday's tilt at Michigan. There's still a lot to like about an elite-coached squad that's going to be a tough out in December. Despite the loss to Ohio State, I'm slotting Indiana above the Buckeyes at this point given the injury to Julian Sayin.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kentucky (6-1) Graced with an intellectual at quarterback and a first-year coach who might be the most confident leader in the FBS not named Curt Cignetti, the Wildcats are legit. There were doubts when this team trailed 17-0 at South Carolina and more when they lined up for the win against LSU the following week in overtime, but Will Stein delivers, man. Saturday's victory at Oklahoma might've been this squad's best given the setup -- a road underdog against a team coming off a rivalry victory over Texas in Red River. And Kentucky came through.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ohio State (6-1) The Buckeyes aren't in that top group because of Sayin's injury, a considerable unknown moving forward this season. It's up to backup Luke Fahey to keep Ohio State on track in the Big Ten picture and CFP conversation, with matchups left to play against USC, Oregon and Northwestern, among others. When you're equipped with Jeremiah Smith and an elite defense, you always have a chance, but the Buckeyes have been downgraded without QB1.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ole Miss (5-1) Pete Golding got his team's attention during their bye week earlier this month after a loss in Gainesville muddied up the hot start and revealed warts. Ole Miss has looked light years better defensively over the last two weekends, culminating with the Rebels' 28-point swat of Missouri in Week 7. They're a betting underdog Saturday at Texas, still have to play fifth-ranked Georgia and travel to Oklahoma before the Egg Bowl. Trinidad Chambliss, after what he showed during last season's CFP, is a warrior and gives Ole Miss a chance to win every game the rest of the season.Tier C.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Alabama (5-2) Outside of Texas, no team's stock has tanked faster than Alabama's over the last two games. Alabama hasn't scored a second-half point since Oct. 3 when the Crimson Tide humiliated Mississippi State, 56-23. Since then, the offense has been kept in check by Georgia and Tennessee, leading to jeers for Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb. The upcoming showdown at LSU next month could determine the SEC's final at-large CFP entry.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU (5-2) Lane Kiffin's team hasn't exhausted their CFP chances just yet, and they could make a Miami-like impact as a high seed if they get there. The Tigers don't need another reminder of their ceiling. They need to start living there and playing with a better sense of urgency. The overtime loss at Kentucky still stings. However, win the games ahead -- especially Alabama -- and CFP seeding takes care of itself. This defense changes considerably without Princewill Umanmielen, so his return is vital.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tennessee (6-1) Jim Knowles is earning every penny of his $2 million salary as the Vols' defensive coordinator. He has fixed just about every problem that Josh Heupel asked of him, and Tennessee has a chance to win the SEC as a result. Last weekend's performance against Alabama was one of the most notable defensive game plans across the sport this fall as the Vols harassed Keelon Russell throughout. Independent of quarterback questions right now, Tennessee has the defense and run game with DeSean Bishop to make a run.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas Tech (6-0) Multiple Big 12 teams may appear in this season's CFP, but are any of the three frontrunners in the conference capable of winning a national championship? The Red Raiders got a first-place vote in the Week 8 AP poll following their destruction of Arizona State and only face one more ranked opponent -- Arizona -- down the stretch. Like last season, Texas Tech will be largely untested when the CFP begins unless it wins a conference title in December against a top-10 foe.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    UCLA (6-0)Defense wins championships, and this unit is humming in Los Angeles. Bob Chesney has flexed his coaching chops in Year 1 with the Bruins, instituting his own version of murder ball at the line of scrimmage. There's nothing sexy about UCLA -- it just keeps winning and taking advantage of one of the Big Ten's most favorable slates. The victory at Oregon was meaningful, but the rivalry finale against USC is the showdown that will be season-defining.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Utah (6-0) Morgan Scalley knows it's easier to overlook issues after wins, but you can bet the Utes' coaching staff will work tirelessly this week to correct the mistakes suffered during last week's win at Colorado. That same performance against Houston on Saturday, two weeks from now against BYU or even at Arizona in November, would crash the season.Tier D.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida (5-2) The Gators got a big win at Texas last week, but Florida still has problems. Defensively, the Gators have been a mess in SEC play. Jon Sumrall continues to harp on the challenges of building a program and the inconsistencies that are bound to persist. At least he knows Florida has two quarterbacks capable of winning games against quality opponents. If they could get the failure-to-show against South Carolina back, the Gators' national outlook would be much different.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Houston (6-1) Conner Weigman has thrown 20 touchdowns this season and accounted for five total scores during last week's win against Oklahoma State. The Cougars can score in a hurry, and their only loss was a disputed failed two-point conversion at Texas Tech in September. This team's dangerous and gets Utah this weekend.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Iowa (5-1) Ten wins might not be enough to reach the CFP as an at-large selection given this strength of schedule, so the Hawkeyes need to run the table from here. The only ranked opponent left is Northwestern on the road come Nov. 7, so it's possible. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Missouri (5-2) Scoring only three points at Ole Miss is really unexplainable when you consider the Tigers were coming off consecutive 200-yard performances from Jamal Roberts on the ground, with quarterback play from Austin Simmons that trounced most others inside the top 25. It felt like the air got let out of the balloon in Oxford, and it's unclear if Missouri can get it back.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas (4-2) There's no excuse for what's going down on the Forty Acres. From No. 1 to almost outside the top 20 over the last two games, offensive struggles continue to damage the Longhorns' title chances under Steve Sarkisian. He can't get it figured out with Arch Manning, it seems. There's no dominant rushing attack despite offseason acquisitions, and now, the Longhorns must battle Ole Miss and potentially others over the next few games without their top defensive player. The roster is handsomely paid and talented, but the coaching isn't good enough here across the board to win it all.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    USC (6-1) The conversation changes if the Trojans beat Ohio State in Week 8, but for now, there's no convincing anyone that Lincoln Riley can beat a quality opponent in the Big Ten until he actually does it. Given Oregon's struggles, USC has to look back at that home loss as a missed opportunity given the talent on this year's team.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wake Forest (6-1) Bob Chesney and Will Stein are crowding the coach-of-the-year buzz and rightfully so, but what Jake Dickert has done with a ragtag roster in the ACC is truly impressive. Wake Forest has spent considerably less money on its roster compared to UCLA and Kentucky, but is on a tear since its only loss of the season -- a 33-20 setback to Miami back on Sept. 18. If the Demon Deacons beat SMU in Dallas in November, they're heading toward an 11-1 finish and a berth in the ACC title game. Who saw that coming?

Halfway through the 2026 college football season, the Big Ten has produced its share of surprises. UCLA and Northwestern are vying for spots in Indianapolis while Oregon and Penn State are just trying to get their seasons back on track.Let's talk about those Bruins. They've aced every single test they've faced in Year 1 under Bob Chesney. A road trip to Eugene? Win. Hosting Wisconsin with backup Ty Dieffenbach starting in place of the injured Nico Iamaleava? Win. The defense has taken immense strides, setting UCLA up to do real damage down the stretch.On the other side of the country and conference, another first-year coach is having the opposite experience. Matt Campbell is still looking for his first Big Ten win at Penn State, and the Nittany Lions have totally squandered what appeared to be one of the softest schedules in the Power Four. To make matters worse, fifth-year senior Rocco Becht was supposed to provide a high floor at quarterback, but the offense has been stuck in the mud for weeks now.There are a couple more overachievers (Northwestern and Iowa), but the conference is filled with teams who have yet to impress. That group includes marquee brands like Michigan, Oregon and Washington.
Before we kick off the second half of the season, I channeled my inner teacher and doled out grades to each Big Ten team. I can empathize with those on the wrong end of the grading curve.

    IllinoisRecord: 3-3, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe Illini defense has gotten worse over the last couple of years, and this year's unit is a major problem (in the bad way). Illinois is a bottom-five Big Ten team in yards allowed per game (375.2), passing yards per game (248.3) and points allowed per game (27.8). The Illini defense also ranked 111th nationally in yards allowed per play at 6.46. I mean, Illinois gave up 37 points to Michigan State! To make matters worse, the offense could be limited moving forward with Katin Houser undergoing hand surgery. Can Illinois scrape together three more wins and reach a bowl? Grade: D+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 IndianaRecord: 6-1, 3-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 6We are using a sliding scale today; otherwise, Indiana would probably have higher marks at 6-1 with a four-point loss to Ohio State as the only blemish. If Nick Marsh gets his foot in bounds, the Hoosiers are undefeated and looking at an "A." It's a game of inches. Having said all that, Indiana still faces a few questions. The offense really lit up the scoreboard in the first five games against overwhelmed opponents, but it scored 35 points in the last two games combined. Josh Hoover has missed on some throws, and the run game has really leveled off after a hot start. Grade: B+

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 15 IowaRecord: 5-1, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 22Iowa has put itself in an excellent position to make a run at the College Football Playoff. There's no shame in a 17-point loss to Ohio State, and with the Hawkeyes sitting at 5-1, the path is wide open. At the moment, Iowa is set to face exactly one ranked team -- No. 24 Northwestern -- the rest of the way. Led by a strong run game, the Iowa offense has been quite effective, and the defense remains stout. Jeremy Hecklinski started at quarterback against Washington, and he threw for three touchdowns and 10.6 yards per attempt in a 41-point effort. If Hecklinski elevates the passing game, watch out for Iowa. Grade: A
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MarylandRecord: 2-5, 0-4 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AOur expectations were already pretty low, and then Maryland lost to Rutgers at home. Mike Locksley entered the season on the hot seat after two consecutive 4-8 seasons, but a 2-5 start this fall cost him his job. Four wins sound pretty good right about now. The offense hasn't been great -- and Malik Washington has disappointed -- but the defense is atrocious. The Terrapins allow an average of 33.3 points per game, which is 127th in the country. Maryland also fired defensive coordinator Ted Monachino after that loss to the Scarlet Knights. Can they be fixed this year? Grade: F
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MichiganRecord: 4-2, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 16By just about every possible metric, Michigan's offense is meaningfully worse than it was last year. That's saying something because the Wolverines weren't exactly lighting it up last fall. Bryce Underwood has regressed, and Kyle Whittingham finally benched him in last week's win over Penn State. Freshman quarterback Tommy Carr gave the offense a spark it had been looking for, and hopefully that's a sign of things to come because the defense is too good to waste. If Whittingham can't get the offense fixed, Michigan will be scrapping to reach a bowl, and there's a possibility he could be one-and-done. Grade: D+

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Michigan StateRecord: 2-5, 0-4 | Preseason AP ranking: N/APat Fitzgerald's second stint in the Big Ten isn't off to an encouraging start. The Spartans are the only Big Ten team that finds the end zone less frequently than Michigan, averaging 21.3 points per game, and there appears to be no end in sight for those woes. As a result, Michigan State is 0-4 in Big Ten play, and the easiest portion of the team's schedule is in the rearview mirror. Road trips to UCLA and Michigan are up next, followed by home games against Washington and Oregon. If you're looking for a silver lining, the Spartans are getting closer. They've lost their last two games by a combined four points. Grade: D-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MinnesotaRecord: 4-2, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe Golden Gophers have a road win over Washington and a home win over Michigan, but they've also been dismantled by Mississippi State and Purdue. That type of inconsistency is what you get when the program does the bare minimum in NIL spending. Drake Lindsey has been a bit disappointing at quarterback, but in his defense, there aren't many difference-makers around him. Minnesota is on track to finish 6-6 or 7-5. It's a perfectly middle-of-the-pack Big Ten team, and the grade reflects that. Grade: C
                            
    
                                                
                    
    NebraskaRecord: 5-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AIf I told you before the season that Nebraska would be 5-2 -- and its losses to Indiana and Oregon would come by a combined six points -- you'd probably be encouraged. Fast-forward to the present day, and it just feels like the same old Nebraska. The Huskers led well into the fourth quarter of both games, and they couldn't hold on for a win. That Dylan Raiola came off the bench to lead a game-winning drive for the middling Ducks only adds salt to the wound. Was the Huskers' 5-0 start a product of its soft schedule, or have they made meaningful progress under Matt Rhule? We'll find out in the second half. Grade: C

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 24 NorthwesternRecord: 5-1, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AHe's been overshadowed by Bob Chesney and Will Stein, but David Braun absolutely deserves consideration for Coach of the Year. Braun's decision to bring in Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator is paying off in spades. The Wildcats offense, which was among the worst in the country last season, is among the most efficient in 2026. Northwestern ranks sixth in the Big Ten in yards per game (424.5), and it ranks third nationally in adjusted EPA per play (0.21). The Wildcats have the chance to reach 6-1 against Rutgers on Saturday. Grade: A+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 Ohio StateRecord: 6-1, 4-0 | Preseason AP ranking: 1The Buckeyes are one bad quarter away from being 7-0 with a pair of top-five wins on their resume. Jeremiah Smith is the best player in college football, and he seems like the runaway favorite to win the Heisman Trophy. The defense has settled in after a somewhat underwhelming start. That's all good, but Ohio State hasn't made life easy on itself. The run game hasn't been dominant, and no one aside from Smith has asserted themselves in the passing game. Now Julian Sayin is dealing with an injury to his throwing shoulder, and the Buckeyes offense may struggle in the coming weeks, but I can only grade what's happened to this point. Grade: A-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    OregonRecord: 4-2, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 2Oregon is in a three-horse race with Texas and Penn State for the honor of being the most disappointing team in college football, and it's currently winning. Dan Lanning's decision to promote from within for coordinator positions has been a misstep, especially regarding offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Dylan Raiola was supposed to be the best backup quarterback in the sport, but that hasn't panned out either. As a result, a team that began the season as national title favorites may miss the College Football Playoff altogether. The only reason the Ducks avoided a failing grade is that they managed to pull out wins over USC and Nebraska without Dante Moore. Grade: D-

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Penn StateRecord: 3-4, 0-4 | Preseason AP ranking: 18Could the Matt Campbell era at Penn State have started any worse? With the exception of losing a non-conference game as a heavy favorite, no. We're more than halfway through October, and the Nittany Lions are still looking for their first conference win. Penn State's four losses to this point include a home defeat at the hands of a middling Wisconsin team, a humiliation against Northwestern and a loss to a Michigan team that used a freshman quarterback. The Nittany Lions' manageable schedule was a reason to buy into this squad in the preseason, but now I'm wondering whether they'll even reach a bowl. To make matters worse, Campbell may have to consider benching fifth-year quarterback Rocco Becht, who followed him from Iowa State. Grade: F
                            
    
                                                
                    
    PurdueRecord: 3-4, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AAfter posting three combined wins in 2024 and 2025, Purdue has already hit that number in the 2026 season. Quarterback Ryan Browne has taken a noticeable step forward and commands a dangerous Boilermakers passing attack, but don't sleep on the ground game. Purdue ran roughshod over Minnesota for 305 yards in a 41-13 rout. The defense is still a work in progress, to put it kindly, but you can't deny that this team has made tangible progress. The schedule will make it tough to reach a bowl, but the Boilermakers could get there if they go 3-0 against Penn State, Maryland and Wisconsin. Grade: B
                            
    
                                                
                    
    RutgersRecord: 2-4, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/ALosing to UMass in Week 1 was a pretty good omen for how this season was going to go. A loss to Boston College in Week 2 really cemented Rutgers' fate. The defense in particular is an abomination -- and yet it's a marginal upgrade over last season's unit. The Scarlet Knights are allowing 402.5 yards and 31.8 points per game, and the offense simply isn't capable of keeping up with opponents, although KJ Duff is a superstar stuck in a bad situation. Greg Schiano's second stint in Piscataway may have run its course, but at least Rutgers got on the board with a Big Ten win over Maryland. Grade: D-

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 UCLARecord: 6-0, 4-0 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AWhen the Bruins hired Bob Chesney, most everyone expected immediate improvement over the team's 3-9 record in 2025. I don't think anyone saw a 6-0 start and a top-10 ranking coming. The most impressive part of UCLA's immediate turnaround under Chesney has to be the defense. Last season, the Bruins allowed 33.4 points per game, which ranked 133rd nationally. That number has dropped by nearly 20 points to 16.2 points per game, which ranks 22nd. Whatever happens the rest of the way, the future is extremely bright in Westwood. Grade: A+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 16 USCRecord: 6-1, 3-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 14Lincoln Riley has his team in position to challenge for a College Football Playoff spot at 6-1, and the offense has been humming with Jayden Maiava at the helm. Only Ohio State is averaging more yards per game, and the Trojans rank fourth in the conference in scoring offense at 36.4 points per game. That said, the defense is a serious concern, and the schedule has been incredibly soft thus far. USC has yet to beat a ranked opponent, and the only ranked team it faced was No. 20 Oregon, which had to replace an injured Dante Moore with Dylan Raiola in the first half. USC's home stretch is much tougher, and it starts this weekend with a road trip to Wisconsin. Grade: B
                            
    
                                                
                    
    WashingtonRecord: 4-3, 1-3 | Preseason AP ranking: 17Coming off a nine-win season in 2025, Washington seemed like it could be a team on the rise, especially with Demond Williams Jr. returning. Thus far, it's been a struggle for the Huskies. They haven't been able to run the football at all, which has put more weight on Williams' shoulders, who is now banged up after an uneven start. The defense has been middling overall, but it's had some really tough performances in Big Ten play. The worst came in a 41-24 loss to Iowa in which the Huskies allowed the Hawkeyes to pile up 465 yards with Jeremy Hecklinski at quarterback. Grade: D+

                            
    
                                                
                    
    WisconsinRecord: 4-2, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe Badgers have already matched last season's win total of four as Luke Fickell aims to cool a seat that was rather warm entering Week 1. The addition of Colton Joseph at quarterback has produced mixed results, but it's hard to argue with what the defense has done, for the most part. Wisconsin is giving up just 16.2 points and 286.7 yards per game. The lack of a reliable offense cost the Badgers a potential win over No. 12 UCLA last weekend, but the team has a major bounce-back opportunity as 16th-ranked USC comes to town. If Wisconsin can emerge victorious, eight or nine wins could be on the table. Grade: B-

title: Quenton Nelson trade destinations: Five potential landing spots for Colts All-Pro guard - CBS Sports
description: Nelson is Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard in 2026, and he is a pending free agent whose general manager
body:
Nelson is Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard in 2026, and he is a pending free agent whose general manager just got fired
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon just signaled to the rest of the NFL that they are set to undergo a rebuild after firing general manager Chris Ballard.Irsay-Gordon ended Ballard's regime six games into his 10th year in charge. Indianapolis reached the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips under Ballard. The Colts' 72-82-1 regular-season record under his management ranked 17th in the league, middle of the pack, during Ballard's tenure. Indianapolis' five missed playoffs in a row represent the Colts' longest such streak in four decades. Indianapolis never won an AFC South title under Ballard.Now, the Colts are set to start over in 2027 with a teardown and rebuild ahead under a new front office. The pro of starting a rebuild now is that the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most talented in years. The con is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick, thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, along with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, to the New York Jets last season in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner.So who could Indianapolis trade away to recoup first-round pick or second-round pick value? Well, Quenton Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler, is set to become one of the NFL's most desired free agents ahead of his 31st birthday. This year, Nelson is Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard with an 89.2 offensive grade.   
He is a coveted, win-now asset who could net Indianapolis a second-round pick or maybe a first-round choice if the bidding for him heats up by the trade deadline on Nov. 10, just a few weeks away. The issue with a potential compensation package for the Colts is that Nelson would be a rental or command a top-of-the-market extension for whoever trades for him.So who could line up to be Nelson's new NFL landing spot? 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York GiantsRecord: 3-2-1 (First in NFC East)It appeared as though the New York Giants' 2026 season was cooked with Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns going down in the first three weeks of the season. Fast forward to the end of the first third of the year, and the Giants remain in first place in the NFC East because it's the NFC Least. This year's NFC East became the first division ever to go winless in consecutive weeks. That means even with J.J. McCarthy starting, the Giants still have a chance to win the division. With Dart still on his rookie deal for two more seasons in 2027 and 2028 before hitting his fifth-year option in 2029, the Giants could take a swing for Nelson in an attempt to win now and begin wooing him for the long haul ahead of his free agency next spring.
Do you know the last time a Giants interior offensive lineman made the Pro Bowl? It was all the way back in 2012 that guard Chris Snee earned the honor, when the world was a much, much different place. Trading for Nelson could be a perfect fit for New York to fix a long-time weakness, and they could structure an extension for him in a way that perfectly lines up with Dart's rookie deal. It doesn't hurt that Nelson is a New Jersey guy, starring at Red Bank (N.J.) Catholic before he enrolled at Notre Dame.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsRecord: 5-0 (First in NFC North)  The Minnesota Vikings' offense needs a boost. Their 5-0 start has almost nothing to do with what they're doing on that side of the ball. They have scored the fewest touchdowns, nine, in a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers, per CBS Sports Research. Their 283.0 total yards per game, which ranks as the sixth-fewest in the NFL this season, is the worst team offense in a 5-0 start since the 1977 Denver Broncos, according to CBS Sports Research. They could be interested if they want to upgrade their offense and move off of undrafted free agent Joe Huber at left guard, with Donovan Jackson out for the season with a torn meniscus. Minnesota will have a phenomenal opportunity to scout Nelson in Week 7 when he and the Colts come to town to play the Vikings.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay PackersRecord: 4-2 (Second in NFC North)    The Green Bay Packers, a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued front, have stabilized their offensive line with the same starting five combination for the last three weeks. That has been a game-changer for them, as that stabilization coincides with their current three-game winning streak. But they could be in the mix, since they're rolling with aging veterans they signed off the street to start for them. Guard Laken Tomlinson, 34, is in his 12th NFL season, and 2024 sixth-round pick guard Travis Glover likely isn't a long-term solution.Nelson is, and when the Packers can protect quarterback Jordan Love and prevent him from being pressured in the pocket, he is a markedly better quarterback. Green Bay is also quietly in an all-in window the next three years, given the structure of Micah Parsons' four-year, $186 million contract with $136 million guaranteed. Yes, the Packers don't have a 2027 first-round pick because of their trade of Parsons, but they do have the rights to their 2027 second- and third-round picks. Plus, they own their top five picks in 2028, so they could muster up a competitive package of picks to trade for Nelson. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ersRecord: 6-0 (First in NFC West)      The San Francisco 49ers could make an all-in trade for Nelson. Quarterback Brock Purdy is playing like the best quarterback in football through the first six weeks of the 2026 season despite a litany of wide receiver injuries. With many of San Francisco's best players on the wrong side of 30 years old, the time is now for the 49ers to contend. 
They are armed with all of their 2027 draft picks through the first five rounds of the draft, and they currently have the most remaining camp space in the entire NFL this season at $41.3 million. San Francisco could get creative with the structure of a potential extension for Nelson. Investing in Nelson could also prolong the career of 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Christian McCaffrey, who is now 30 years old with plenty of tread on his tires. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Houston TexansRecord: 2-4 (Third in AFC South)        If the Houston Texans (2-4), winners of two in a row, continue to climb, perhaps they would be interested. However, their asking price from the Colts could be higher since they're a fellow AFC South team. Being able to replace Ed Ingram, Pro Football Focus' No. 26-graded guard with a 69.1 offensive grade, with PFF's No. 1 guard could be a major boon for ascending quarterback C.J. Stroud. He ranks second in the NFL in passing yards (1,714), third in touchdown-to-interception ratio (9-1), 11th in passer rating (100.9), and tied for first in 20-yard completions (25) for a Texans squad that has now won two in a row after an 0-4 start. Imagine how much higher he and Houston could soar with Nelson blocking for him in pursuit of a third AFC South title in four years.
